source.title: The Implicit Bias of Batch Normalization in Linear Models and Two-layer Linear Convolutional Neural Networks
source.authors: Yuan Cao; Difan Zou; Yuan-Fang Li; Quanquan Gu

record.file_problem: not stated; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves training-loss convergence for linear models with batch normalization, addressing whether gradient training can fit the training data through a different, theoretical method and in narrower settings than the version describes.
record.gate_note: The paper's VGG-16 experiment measures margin uniformity, not training classification error, so it is not a row. Comparisons to no-BN results in prior work are cited findings, not this study's own results.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional convergence for batch-normalized linear models and single-filter linear CNNs, rather than testing V1's nonlinear CNN training on CIFAR-10/100. Its BN speed comparison concerns convergence of weight direction toward different margin solutions, not V6's accuracy gains or learning-rate tolerance. No own result tests V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under the stated assumptions, gradient descent with BN achieves vanishing training loss and converges toward uniform margins in linear models and patch-wise uniform margins in two-layer single-filter linear CNNs. The fast exp(-Ω(log² t)) rate concerns margin discrepancy; training loss decays as Θ(1/t) for fixed learning rate and patch count.
record.recipe_differences: The results are theoretical analyses of full-batch gradient descent on cross-entropy loss for batch-normalized linear models, rather than empirical benchmark training of nonlinear CNNs with SGD or Adam.
record.method_sensitivity: The theorems require a separable uniform-margin solution and sufficiently small initialization scale and learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the stated solvability, initialization and learning-rate assumptions, training loss tends to zero for both model classes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full-batch gradient descent can perfectly fit data admitting uniform-margin solutions using batch-normalized linear classifiers and single-filter linear CNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: Margin discrepancy converges at exp(-Ω(log² t)); the authors compare this directional convergence with previously established maximum-margin convergence without BN. Figures 1 and 2 examine margin uniformity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization changes implicit bias toward uniform margins and can accelerate directional convergence in the analyzed linear settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Two constructed learning problems give better test-error guarantees for patch-wise uniform-margin classifiers than maximum-margin classifiers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN's patch-wise uniform-margin bias can improve generalization in particular synthetic learning problems.

record.problems: The training-fit results are theoretical and conditional on stated assumptions; they do not establish behavior on the nonlinear benchmark networks and datasets in V1. The paper's CIFAR-10 VGG-16 experiment reports margin uniformity rather than training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: The VGG-16 with/without batch normalization experiment in Figure 2 measures margin uniformity on cat and dog classes, not training error, so it does not qualify as a row for the claim versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error of sufficiently large nonlinear CNNs on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels, and dependence on size, stopping and regularization.
Spurious minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Comparative effects of activation-matched initialization on learning speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to a learning-rate stability threshold.
BN's effects on accuracy acquisition and tolerable learning rates, and Fixup's comparative training speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V1 limits_scope verdict: studying different systems and leaving benchmark conditions untested does not demonstrate a limitation of V1. The introduction's claims about BN accelerating optimization cite prior work.

versions.untested_parts: The paper studies linear models and two-layer, single-filter linear CNNs with batch normalization under separability and small-initialization and learning-rate assumptions. It does not test nonlinear convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, SGD or Adam benchmark recipes, or the effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
